questions.q: What does a dashboard's "running user" determine?
options: Who is allowed to edit the dashboard
Whose record-level data access determines what shows up in the dashboard
Which folder the dashboard is saved in
How often the dashboard refreshes
questions.explain: The running user's data access is what actually produces the numbers and records shown. Everything displayed reflects what that person, specifically, is allowed to see.

questions.q: What does setting View Dashboard As to "The Dashboard Viewer" do?
options: It makes the dashboard read-only for everyone
It makes the running user whoever is currently viewing the dashboard, instead of one fixed person
It hides the dashboard from all folders
It converts every report on the dashboard into a Joined report
questions.explain: This is the setting that creates a dynamic dashboard — each viewer's own access determines what they see, rather than everyone seeing one fixed person's data access.

questions.q: What on-screen text indicates a dashboard is dynamic?
options: A red "Dynamic" badge in the folder list
"Viewing as [Name] · Change" under the dashboard header
A lock icon next to the dashboard title
Nothing is shown; it can only be confirmed in Setup
questions.explain: A dynamic dashboard displays "Viewing as [Name]" with a Change link right under the header, showing which running user's access is currently being reflected.

questions.q: Where can a dynamic dashboard NOT be saved?
options: A folder shared with a public group
A folder shared with a specific role
A private folder
A folder shared with All Internal Users
questions.explain: A dynamic dashboard needs to be seen by multiple people running as themselves, which requires a shared folder — it can't be saved in a private folder, which by definition only the owner can access.

questions.q: A VP wants one dashboard that forty reps can each open to see only their own pipeline, without building 40 separate dashboards. Why would a static dashboard fail here?
options: Static dashboards can't contain funnel charts
A static dashboard always shows one fixed running user's data access to every viewer, regardless of who's actually looking
Static dashboards can only be viewed by administrators
Static dashboards don't support folder sharing at all
questions.explain: A static dashboard shows the same running user's data to everyone who opens it, so all forty reps would see the same person's pipeline instead of their own. A dynamic dashboard solves this with one definition, viewer-by-viewer.
